messages:
maria: Heads-up — incoming alert: analytics-service role appears to have been able to Decrypt a customer CMK used for embeddings. Noted by alerting rule 'kms-customer-decrypts' at 14:02 UTC. This looks like it started right after the RBAC role refactor last night.
ops-bot: [ALERT] kms-customer-decrypts triggered for arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-... by principal arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/analytics-service-role/session -> CloudTrail event: Decrypt.
kevin: ack. can we confirm scope — single key or broad access? any cross-account principals?
maria: quick check from CloudTrail shows Decrypt for key alias/customer/embeddings-01 and principal is analytics-service-role in our account. No obvious cross-account ARN in this log line, but the key is customer-managed and supposed to be restricted to the private-deploy worker nodes.
sri: timeline? RBAC change pushed at 02:10 UTC. Which commit/PR?
jess: PR #8123 merged 02:07 UTC — role -> service-role refactor. Policy consolidation moved a few managed policies onto analytics-service-role. Suspect a policy regression.
kevin: immediate mitigations: 1) remove kms:Decrypt from analytics-service-role, 2) revoke any active STS sessions for that role, 3) rotate key if there's evidence of exfil. Who can run the revoke now?
maria: I can remove the policy binding quickly. Running: 
```
# detach managed policy from role
aws iam detach-role-policy --role-name analytics-service-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/Redwood-Analytics-FullAccess
# list inline policies
aws iam list-role-policies --role-name analytics-service-role
```
kevin: hold on — if we detach full access we might break live pipelines. Do it in a safe window but we need immediate containment. Alternative: add an explicit deny statement scoped to kms:Decrypt on that key. That will be abrupt but reversible.
sri: good call. Add a deny policy at the role level referencing the key ARN. Example deny: 
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Deny",
      "Action": "kms:Decrypt",
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-...",
      "Condition": {"Bool": {"aws:PrincipalIsAWSService": "false"}}
    }
  ]
}
```
jess: I'm OK applying that deny now. Doing it via console/cli and keeping a timestamped backup for rollback.
maria: applied deny at 14:12 UTC. Confirming no further Decrypt events after that in the last 3 minutes.
audit-bot: CloudTrail note: Decrypt events for key/abcd-... at 14:02, 14:05, 14:07 by analytics-service-role. No external IPs detected in those calls.
kevin: good containment. Next: audit list of principals with kms:Decrypt on customer keys — run this across account. Use: 
```
aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/analytics-service-role --action-names kms:Decrypt --resource-arns arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-...
```
and to enumerate grants on the CMK: 
```
aws kms list-grants --key-id abcd-... --limit 50
```
sri: I ran list-grants and found a grant to a legacy service principal `analytics-legacy-agent` that should have been revoked during migration. That grant included Decrypt. Looks like the refactor re-attached a managed policy which granted AssumeRole into legacy principal indirectly.
jess: oof. So there are two issues: 1) managed policy attached to analytics-service-role reintroduced path to the grant, 2) lingering KMS grant directly allowed Decrypt. We need to retire the grant and remove the assume path. Plan: retire grant now, revoke role sessions, revert policy consolidation for analytics until we have a clean IAM mapping.\eops: note, retiring a grant doesn't prevent existing ciphertext already decrypted. We need to assume potential exposure window 02:07–14:12 UTC.\kevin: timeline + customer comms: SRE/security needs to estimate affected customer keys and whether any plaintext left the account. Ask logs team for S3 PUTs or network egress correlated with Decrypt events.\maria: pinging logs team — @jordan-logs can you run a query for any PutObject/SendToExternal endpoints within those session IDs from 02:07–14:12? include container IDs.
kevin: practical steps now: 
- retire KMS grant(s): `aws kms retire-grant --grant-id <id> --key-id abcd-...`
- revoke role sessions: `aws sts revoke-session` (we'll use aws-iam-authenticator tooling to kill tokens)
- create a temporary key alias and rekey customer data if we detect exfil
- schedule a full key rotation for the CMK and search for decrypted plaintext in logs

Can we get a volunteer to run retire-grant + revoke sessions?
sri: I'll run retire-grant after jess posts grant IDs. Then I'll run `aws iam list-role-policies` and `aws sts get-session-token` audit to enumerate active sessions.
jess: grant IDs: G-1a2b3c4d, G-5e6f7g8h. Retiring G-1a2b3c4d now.
ops-bot: [ACTION] retire-grant G-1a2b3c4d on key/abcd-... completed at 14:22 UTC.
sri: revoked role sessions for analytics-service-role at 14:25 UTC. Confirmed new STS tokens failing Decrypt due to deny.
audit-bot: CloudTrail re-check: no new Decrypts after 14:12. All retired grants logged at 14:22.
kevin: next postmortem checklist: 
- root cause: IAM policy merge reintroduced legacy assume path + leftover KMS grant.
- immediate remediation: deny + retire grants + revoke sessions (done).
- medium-term: revert PR #8123 and open a follow-up to split policies by least privilege.
- keys: schedule rotation and re-encrypt customer datasets where feasible; offer customers a transparency note if necessary.
- monitoring: add an alert for any Decrypt by analytics-service-role on customer CMKs (already had one but need to tie to PR merges).
maria: I'll open incident doc and start a customer impact assessment. Creating: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-2026-kms-access (draft).
sri: also propose an automated check in CI that fails PRs that assign managed policy `Redwood-Analytics-FullAccess` to any role together with `AssumeRole` trust to legacy agents.
jess: agreed. I'll revert the merge and cut a scoped patch to remove `Redwood-Analytics-FullAccess` from analytics-service-role.
kevin: thanks team. keep this thread for updates. If logs team finds evidence of external exfil, escalate to legal/comms. 
maria: closing containment phase. Will update with re-encryption timeline and any affected customers. :lock:
